newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse December turnover slumps.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse December turnover slumps.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) December turnover fell to 119.089 million dinars ($23.2 million) from 152.52 million in November, the bourse said on Tuesday.
The number of deals rose to 738 from 702 a month ago.
"This was not a bad result for December when liquidity of the banking sector plunged dramatically," BSE managing director Pava Zecevic told Reuters.
The total 1996 turnover rose to 2.186 billion dinars, slightly falling short of estimated 2.2 billion dinars.
Commercial paper traded 601 times for a volume of 83.835 million dinars.
Those were followed by the central bank short-term bonds. The bonds saw five deals worth 16.02 million dinars.
Treasury bills were traded 114 times for a volume of 13.436 million dinars.
The BSE reported eight deals in wheat forward contracts worth 4.274 million dinars.
Certificates of deposit and giro money transactions, with banks trading their surplus liquidity, accounted for the rest of the December total.
Zecevic did not expect the market to pick up in January, for most banks and companies will be closed for New Year and Christmas holidays until January 8.
But she expressed hope that January will bring the first trade of shares on the Belgrade bourse.
"We are currently negotiating with several banks planning to list their shares on BSE," she said.
The Belgrade bourse has not traded any equities over past two years. Two shares -- by Investbanka and Sintelon -- were listed but never traded and earlier this year withdrawn.
However, sources close to the BSE said AIK Banka Nis placed 20.5 million dinars of its stock on the bourse earlier this week. The buyer was one of the leading Yugoslav banks.
The bourse would not comment on the sale until it was finalised through its clearing department. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
